correctness.rationale: The attack dependency DAG gives a finite topological induction. For any complete extension E, an already-fired attack forces exclusion by conflict-freeness, while a nonfired attack has a rejected predecessor attacked by E, so every closed attacker of a candidate-included vertex is attacked and completeness forces inclusion. For any stable E, no inactive attack can leave a vertex excluded because outsiders must be attacked; both unique possibilities are K. If K is closed, any attacker of a K-member has a K-excluded tail predecessor and is therefore defeated; K is admissible, and every K-outsider has an attack tail T within K whose closed hull lies within K, so cannot be defended. It follows K is complete and stable, hence uniquely grounded. Otherwise closedness precludes all three. No step assumes support acyclicity; 34,455 finite diagnostic checks independently evaluate semantics against the criterion.

value.rationale: Classical BSAF complete semantics can lack extensions due to mandatory supports despite acyclic attacks. The theorem is an exact necessary/sufficient existence classification and linear-time constructive algorithm for all finite frameworks with acyclic collective-attack dependency, allowing unrestricted collective supports including cycles and nullary premises. It provides a sharp existence gate for three semantics simultaneously; the given three-node example shows why preferred semantics does not collapse. This resolves a natural structural/algorithmic subclass rather than a routine parameter increment.
